collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — RELATIONSHIPS, SINGLEHOOD AND FAMILY (FAM2-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Couples of every kind, courting, quarrels, separations without blame, widowhood and second loves, happily single and childfree villagers, single parents, grandparents, siblings, chosen and extended families, and affection that isn't romantic. Nobody has to love, marry or have children, everyone may say no to affection, and a player's choice never obliges a villager to anything.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two children aged 6-10)

collection.description: A child offers a friend flowers and learns they like frogs better: go and find a frog, or keep the flowers.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has picked a big handful of flowers and is holding them out to (friend) with great ceremony. "These are for you," (subject.he/she) says. "Because you're my favorite." (friend) looks at the flowers. Then at (subject). Then, seriously, says, "I like frogs better than flowers."

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) considers this. Then (subject.he/she) puts down the flowers and marches off to the stream. Half an hour later (subject.he/she) comes back, soaked, holding out a small, indignant frog. (friend) is delighted. They spend the afternoon building it a frog house. The frog escapes at once. Neither of them minds. The flowers wilt on a rock, forgotten.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Well, they're still for you," says (subject) firmly. (friend) shrugs and takes them. (friend.He/she) puts them behind (friend.his/her) ear, upside down. Then they go and look for frogs together anyway. By the end of the afternoon they've forgotten all about who is whose favorite. The flowers fall out somewhere near the stream.
